quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: 'Apparently that's my problem' after a failure one month after warranty expiry — what tone is this?
quests.explanation: Sarcastic acceptance of blame for a failure just past warranty expiry is a form of bitter anger.
quests.textToSpeak: The warranty was for two years. It broke at twenty-five months, and apparently that's my problem.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: An unexpected third outcome when two obvious options existed — what does this unexplained result produce?
quests.explanation: An outcome that bypasses both visible options with no explanation produces curiosity about the reasoning.
quests.textToSpeak: Two people applied for the same job — one with a degree but no experience, one with experience but no degree. They hired a third person.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A silent hug as the only response to news — what does this wordless reaction usually communicate?
quests.explanation: A long, silent hug as the only response to news expresses a depth of happiness beyond words.
quests.textToSpeak: She didn't say a word when I told her. She just walked over and hugged me for a very long time.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A family home sold without consultation, witnessed being taken over by strangers — what is this feeling?
quests.explanation: Seeing strangers move into a family home that was sold without discussion produces loss and sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: He sold the family house without discussing it with anyone. I drove past it the day the new owners moved in.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: The least experienced person solving what the most qualified could not — what does this outcome produce?
quests.explanation: A junior employee solving a senior department's two-month problem is a genuinely surprising outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: The most junior member of our team solved a problem the engineering department had been working on for two months.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Familiarity with the setting but feeling like a first-timer anyway — what emotion is interfering here?
quests.explanation: Feeling like a first-timer despite known surroundings is nervousness overriding the comfort of familiarity.
quests.textToSpeak: I know this room and these faces — I've stood here before. Why does it feel like the first time?

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Being unable to think of anything else before a career-defining decision — what emotion is this?
quests.explanation: When a professional dream is being decided in a meeting you can't attend, the resulting focus is excitement.
quests.textToSpeak: The publisher's assistant said my book would be discussed at Tuesday's board meeting. I can't think of anything else.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Four meetings in one day about three items that haven't changed in a month — what has set in completely?
quests.explanation: Repeat meetings about static agenda items with no progress across weeks and multiple sessions is pure boredom.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm on my fourth meeting of the day about the same three agenda items that haven't changed since last month.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: 'Brought me in because they needed someone who knows' — what does this self-description project?
quests.explanation: Being hired for your knowledge and stating it clearly after twenty years of experience is confidence.
quests.textToSpeak: I've worked in this industry for twenty years. They brought me in because they needed someone who knows what they're doing.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A recurring, specific locked door that everyone silently accepts — what does the observer feel?
quests.explanation: A specific, recurring anomaly that no one questions produces natural curiosity in those who notice.
quests.textToSpeak: The door to the break room is always locked on the first Monday of every month. Nobody mentions it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Realizing there's no record of a private moment with someone you cared about — what does this reflect?
quests.explanation: The absence of a single private photo with someone you were close to reflects sadness at what wasn't captured.
quests.textToSpeak: I don't have a single photo of just the two of us. We were always with a group.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Following all instructions perfectly and then being told the system lost it — what emotion is this?
quests.explanation: Doing everything correctly only for a system failure to nullify the effort produces frustration and anger.
quests.textToSpeak: I filed the report correctly, followed every instruction, and now I'm told the submission portal lost it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A morning trip producing food, flowers, and new connections — what emotion underlies this kind of day?
quests.explanation: A spontaneous, fruitful social morning at a market reflects a particularly happy and open state of mind.
quests.textToSpeak: I went to the farmers market and came back with flowers, bread, cheese, and three people's phone numbers.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Counting seconds of someone else's interview beyond its normal length — what emotion does that counting reveal?
quests.explanation: Counting the seconds of an overrun interview for someone you care about shows anxious, nervous concern.
quests.textToSpeak: She's outside the room right now. Her interview started ninety seconds ago, which is forty seconds longer than usual. I'm counting.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A complete reversal from commercial failure to stadium sellout over ten years — what is the reaction?
quests.explanation: Going from cancelled due to poor sales to a stadium sellout is a dramatic turnaround that produces surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: The band that cancelled due to poor ticket sales ten years ago was seen last night selling out a stadium.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A weekly newsletter with identical content about the same topics every time — what has replaced reading it?
quests.explanation: Identical content repeated weekly in a newsletter makes receiving it a source of boredom.
quests.textToSpeak: The company newsletter arrives every Monday and every Monday it says the same things about engagement and core values.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A missed call that turns out to be the final one — what makes this sentence carry such weight?
quests.explanation: Finding out a missed call was the last one carries the weight of irreversible loss and deep sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: My mother called while I was at work. I missed it. It was the last time her number appeared on my screen.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Three simultaneous departures followed by collective social media silence — what pattern does this suggest?
quests.explanation: A synchronized pattern of departure and public silence in three unrelated people suggests a story worth knowing.
quests.textToSpeak: Three people quit the same team in one month and all three immediately stopped updating their social media.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: The same error surviving three corrections — what emotion does repetition of someone else's mistake produce?
quests.explanation: Correcting the same mistake three times with no retention produces clear frustration and anger.
quests.textToSpeak: I've corrected this error in the report three times. Each time it comes back from editing with the same mistake.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: 'Will handle whatever' after months of stress-testing — what level of technical certainty is expressed here?
quests.explanation: Months of systematic stress-testing followed by a categorical claim of readiness expresses confidence.
quests.textToSpeak: We've stress-tested this system for months. It will handle whatever the launch throws at it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Screaming at an early morning call loud enough to alarm a neighbor — what news produces this reaction?
quests.explanation: An early-morning call producing involuntary screaming suggests receiving extremely exciting news.
quests.textToSpeak: The call came in at seven in the morning. I answered half-asleep. I screamed so loud my neighbor knocked on the wall.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: The last box making a new place feel real — why might this moment produce sadness rather than relief?
quests.explanation: The last box finalizing a move can make the distance from home feel permanent, producing sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: I unpacked the last box yesterday. That was when it became real that I was actually living here now.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Twenty years of dereliction replaced by full restoration during one trip — what is the natural reaction?
quests.explanation: Finding a long-derelict building fully restored and functional after an absence produces genuine surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: The building had been derelict for twenty years. I came back from a long trip to find it fully restored and open.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Physical symptoms — dry throat and restlessness — appearing before a performance review — what is this?
quests.explanation: Dry throat and inability to sit still before a performance review are classic physical signs of nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: My manager is about to walk in for my performance review. My throat has gone dry and I can't sit still.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: An unplanned evening that naturally extended into the night — what state produces this kind of ease?
quests.explanation: Staying at a table long after a meal with no plan to do so describes a naturally happy evening.
quests.textToSpeak: We didn't plan anything special. We just ended up staying at the table long after the food was gone, talking.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Two unauthorized payments of the same invoice from different sources with no explanation — what is this?
quests.explanation: A double payment with no authorization from two separate sources is an anomaly that produces curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: The invoice was paid twice by two different people in the same organization. Nobody authorized either payment.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Stopping note-taking after repeated 'exciting updates' with no substance — what does this action signal?
quests.explanation: Giving up on note-taking after repeated content-free updates reveals that boredom has taken over.
quests.textToSpeak: After the fifth 'exciting update' in today's meeting, I stopped writing notes. Nothing has actually changed.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: A card arriving after someone has died, sent before they did — what delayed arrival like this produces?
quests.explanation: Receiving a card from someone who has since died, written when they were still alive, produces deep sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: I got a card in the post this morning. It was dated the week before she passed — it must have been delayed.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Applying at 9 a.m. and finding out by noon that someone was hired without you being considered — what is this?
quests.explanation: Being bypassed within hours of submitting an application without even being considered produces anger.
quests.textToSpeak: I sent the contract at 9 a.m. By noon, I received a call to say they'd already given the job to someone else.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the matching emotion.
quests.hint: Numbers confirming your initial diagnosis three months in — what does validation of your read produce?
quests.explanation: Being proven right by numbers three months after a confident initial assessment reinforces confidence.
quests.textToSpeak: I came into this organization knowing exactly what needed fixing. Three months later, the numbers show I was right.
